# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

An edge controller manages charging at several electric-vehicle connectors supplied by one electrical branch whose allowable aggregate current is lower than the sum of the connector ratings. Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier. A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors. A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus.

The controller stores, for each active connector, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value. At each allocation interval, the controller subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current. It first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit. The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor.

The branch current sensor is an independent safety input. If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval, the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit. A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero, the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command. The controller then inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator.

The controller can receive remote schedules and authorizations through a network interface, but it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory. During a network outage it continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process. It does not start a newly connected session unless the local token authorizes that connector and has not expired. Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns.

A service input permits an installer to associate connector identifiers with physical contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time and confirming the corresponding connector current sensor. The association is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector. This prevents a wiring-map error from assigning a current limit to the wrong connector.

The disclosed essential relationship is closed-loop allocation using both per-connector current sensing and independent upstream branch sensing, with staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond. Offline authorization, welded-contactor isolation, tamper-evident records, and installation mapping are supported additional features.

content.content:
1	Sites that install several electric-vehicle charging connectors frequently supply those connectors from a single electrical branch. The branch is protected at an allowable aggregate current, referred to herein as a branch limit, that is commonly lower than the sum of the individual connector ratings. Installing a branch large enough for every connector to draw its full rating at the same time is often impractical.
2	
3	Charging equipment therefore has to share a fixed amount of current among connectors that could collectively demand more. The signalling mechanism ordinarily available for that purpose is the control pilot presented to each vehicle, which advertises a maximum current that the vehicle is permitted to draw. Control-pilot signalling is advisory in nature. The value advertised on the pilot is a command, not a measurement, and the current actually drawn depends on the behaviour of the vehicle receiving it. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous value, or may not reduce at all. Control that assumes the commanded value is the delivered value therefore has no way to detect the case in which the branch remains loaded above its limit after a reduction has been ordered, and that case is precisely the one in which the branch protective device is at risk of operating and removing service from every connector on the branch.
4	
5	A further difficulty arises because the branch usually carries loads other than charging. Equipment on the same branch other than the charging connectors consumes part of the allowable aggregate current, and that consumption varies through the day. Allocation that divides the full branch limit among the connectors, without accounting for the varying non-charging portion of the branch load, either overcommits the branch or forces the installer to configure a permanently conservative limit that wastes capacity for most of the day.
6	
7	Sharing schemes that divide available current equally, or in proportion to instantaneous request, also tend to treat every session alike. Where sessions have been served unequally over the course of a shared-capacity period, for example because one session began while the branch was heavily loaded and another began while it was lightly loaded, equal division perpetuates the inequality rather than correcting it.
8	
9	Charging equipment is additionally exposed to conditions that are specific to its power path and its installation. A contactor whose contacts have welded continues to pass current after an open command has been issued, so an allocation scheme that treats an open command as removal of the load will continue to believe that capacity has been released when it has not. Site communication to a remote management system is not continuous, so equipment that depends on a remote authority for both authorization and current limits either stops serving vehicles when the link fails or continues without a governing limit. Multi-connector equipment is also wired by hand, and a transposition between the logical identifier of a connector and the physical contactor and sensor channel that serve it causes a current limit intended for one connector to be applied to another, which defeats the allocation entirely while leaving every individual component apparently functional.
10	
11	There remains a need for charging control that treats the current actually present on the branch and at each connector as the governing quantity, that keeps the branch within its limit even when a vehicle does not honour a reduced pilot command, that allocates the genuinely available portion of the branch limit in a way that corrects accumulated inequality between sessions, and that remains safe and operable when the site link is down, when a contactor has welded, and when the installation wiring map has not been independently confirmed.
12

5	FIG. 1 shows a charging control system in which an edge controller 100 manages charging at a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the plurality of connectors. The allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, referred to in this description as the branch limit, is lower than the sum of the ratings of the connectors that the branch conductor 102 supplies. The branch limit is a stored value that corresponds to the aggregate current the branch is permitted to carry.
6	
7	The branch conductor 102 supplies a first connector station 110 and a second connector station 112. Two connector stations are shown for clarity of illustration. The system accommodates a larger plurality of connector stations, and the description of the first connector station 110 applies to each further connector station of the plurality. The branch conductor 102 also supplies a non-charging load 114, which is load on the same branch other than the connector stations.
8	
9	A branch current sensor 104 is located upstream of the contactors of the connector stations and measures the total current on the branch conductor 102. The branch current sensor 104 is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured branch current to it.
10	
11	The edge controller 100 communicates with the connector stations over an isolated local bus 106. The isolated local bus 106 carries assigned current limits and contactor commands from the edge controller 100 to the control-pilot interfaces and the contactors of the connector stations, and carries control-pilot status from the connector stations to the edge controller 100. Each connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured connector current to it. The isolated local bus 106 is isolated between the edge controller 100 and the connector stations.
12	
13	A network interface 108 connects the edge controller 100 to a remote management system. The allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, referred to in this description as the branch limit, is lower than the sum of the ratings of the connectors that the branch conductor 102 supplies. The branch limit is a stored value that corresponds to the aggregate current the branch is permitted to carry.

The branch conductor 102 supplies a first connector station 110 and a second connector station 112. Two connector stations are shown for clarity of illustration. The system accommodates a larger plurality of connector stations, and the description of the first connector station 110 applies to each further connector station of the plurality. The branch conductor 102 also supplies a non-charging load 114, which is load on the same branch other than the connector stations.

A branch current sensor 104 is located upstream of the contactors of the connector stations and measures the total current on the branch conductor 102. The branch current sensor 104 is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured branch current to it.

The edge controller 100 communicates with the connector stations over an isolated local bus 106. The isolated local bus 106 carries assigned current limits and contactor commands from the edge controller 100 to the control-pilot interfaces and the contactors of the connector stations, and carries control-pilot status from the connector stations to the edge controller 100. Each connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured connector current to it. The isolated local bus 106 is isolated between the edge controller 100 and the connector stations.

As described below, the network interface 108 conveys remote schedules and authorizations to the edge controller 100 and conveys uploaded meter records from the edge controller 100, but the safety behaviour of the system does not depend on the availability of the network interface 108.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 100 of FIG. 1 in greater detail. The edge controller 100 is further coupled to the branch current sensor 104 of FIG. 1, over which coupling the branch current sensor 104 reports the measured branch current to the edge controller 100. The edge controller 100 carries out the allocation and protection processes described below. The nonvolatile memory 132 retains stored values across loss of supply.

The edge controller 100 is further coupled to a local fault indicator 134 and to a service input 136. The local fault indicator 134 provides an indication at the equipment itself, independently of the network interface 108. The service input 136 is an input by which an installer initiates the association of connector identifiers with physical contactors described below.

The charging authorization records that the session at that connector is permitted to draw energy. The requested current is a stored value that represents the current requested for the session at that connector. The minimum sustaining current is a stored current value that is assigned to the session at that connector before any further distribution of the available charging current is made. The energy-deficit value is a stored value that represents the energy by which the session at that connector has been under-served.

FIG. 4 shows the process carried out by the edge controller 100. The edge controller 100 repeats the allocation portion of the process at each allocation interval. The allocation interval is a recurring period at which the edge controller 100 revises the assigned limits.

At an available-charging-current determination step 200, the edge controller 100 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the measured portion of the branch current that is drawn by the non-charging load 114. At a minimum sustaining current assignment step 202, the edge controller 100 first assigns the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive it. Sessions with a greater energy-deficit value receive a greater share of the remaining current than sessions with a smaller energy-deficit value.

The branch current sensor 104 is an independent safety input. The reduced pilot command is the first stage of the staged sequence.

At a reclose permissive step 212, the edge controller 100 governs the reclosing of a contactor that has been opened by the ordered contactor shedding step 210. The edge controller 100 does not reclose such a contactor until three conditions are satisfied together: the connector current sensor of that connector reports zero current, the control-pilot interface of that connector reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 100 records a welded-contactor condition for a connector when the connector current measured by the connector current sensor of that connector remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector. The leakage threshold is a current magnitude above zero, so that a connector current that has genuinely ceased is distinguished from a connector current that persists after the open command.

When the welded-contactor condition has been recorded, the edge controller 100 inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates the local fault indicator 134.

Operation during a network outage

The edge controller 100 can receive remote schedules and authorizations through the network interface 108. The edge controller 100 stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory 132. The signed local authorization token authorizes one or more connectors of the plurality and has an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the most recent branch limit that the edge controller 100 has accepted.

During a network outage the edge controller 100 continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process described above. Charging therefore continues through the outage within the last accepted branch limit. During the outage the last accepted branch limit is the branch limit to which the protection process described above is applied, so that the edge controller 100 sends a reduced pilot command and, when the measured branch current remains above the last accepted branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and the verification interval has elapsed, opens the connector contactors one at a time in the stored shedding order. The edge controller 100 does not start a newly connected session unless the signed local authorization token authorizes that connector and has not expired. No session is started at a connector that the signed local authorization token does not authorize, and no session is started at any connector after the token has expired.

Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence held locally by the edge controller 100. The records accumulated during the outage are uploaded when communication returns.

A multi-connector installation is wired by hand, and the identifier a connector is given in configuration must correspond to the physical contactor and the physical current sensor channel that serve that connector. A transposition assigns a current limit intended for one connector to another. Every component continues to function, every sensor continues to report, and the allocation nevertheless governs the wrong power path.

The association between a connector identifier and a physical contactor is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector. If the responding channel is not the channel expected for the commanded connector, or if no channel responds, no association is stored for that connector. The mapping is thus established by measurement on the same sensors that the allocation process later relies upon, so a wiring-map error is found during installation instead of silently misdirecting current limits for the life of the installation.

The allocation process, the branch protection process, the offline authorization behaviour, the welded-contactor isolation, the tamper-evident record sequence, and the installation mapping are described together because they share the sensors and the isolated local bus 106 of a single edge controller 100. They are nevertheless separable. content.text: I've read all inputs, all draft sections, the numeral table, and all four figure briefs, and traced every claim limitation, numbered part, structure, relationship, and operating condition against the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary:
Ledger result: the specification text, claims, abstract, numeral table and three of the four figure briefs trace cleanly to the inventor sources; one untraced drawing topology remains.

Authority used: input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (identical text). The one YOU passage in the conversation is drafting-agent prose and input/request.md is a resume/repair instruction, so neither was treated as inventor support. input/brief.md supplied only the title, applicant/inventor name, absence of a priority claim, and absence of federal sponsorship, all of which match draft/01-title.md, draft/02-cross-reference.md and draft/03-government-support.md.

Traced and clean:
- Claim 1 elements (connector stations with contactor between branch and respective connector, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface presenting an assigned limit; branch current sensor upstream of the contactors; isolated local bus; controller storing branch limit lower than the sum of connector ratings and, per active connector, a charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value; per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve; minimum-sustaining-first then deficit-based distribution; send-on-pilot then verify-with-sensor; reduced pilot command, verification interval, and one-at-a-time shedding in a stored order until branch current is below the branch limit) all map to disclosure paragraphs 1–3.
- Dependent claims 2–9 and method claims 10–16 map one-for-one: reclose permissive triple condition (para. 3), welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold after an open command and the resulting inhibit plus local fault indicator (para. 3), network interface with signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation, refusal to start an unauthorized or expired session, tamper-evident meter-record sequence uploaded on return (para. 4), and service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with storage only after the sensed channel agrees (para. 5). Claims 9 and 16 (re-evaluate between openings, open no further contactor once below the limit) are supported by "opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit".
- All 23 numerals (100–136, 200–214) are defined once in draft/numerals.md, used consistently in draft/08-detailed-description.md, and each designates one part throughout. Every numeral listed on a sheet is defined; every defined numeral appears on a sheet (8/7/8/8). Reuse of 100, 102, 104, 106 and 108 across FIG. 1, FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 is like-parts reuse across views, not conflicting meaning.
- The separability paragraph in the Detailed Description tracks the disclosure's own "Offline authorization, welded-contactor isolation, tamper-evident records, and installation mapping are supported additional features", so it adds no unsupported optional embodiment.
- draft/07-drawings.md matches the four briefs in view type and content; there is no sectional view, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed and no repeated section designation needs to agree across views.
- No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment survives in any draft/ or figures/ file (a text search for such markers hit only .agent/ logs and review/previous-qa.md, neither of which is filing text).
- The FIG. 2 note that the series order of contactor 120 and sensor 122 "is a drawing convention" is properly confined to the figure brief; the specification and claims stay order-neutral, and series order carries no technical substance for a common current. No application sentence anywhere justifies a renderer's choice with "by way of example", "any closed outline" or similar broadening.
- Schematic housings, slabs and page placements (rectangles for stations, controller, memory, indicator, service input; upper-third and lower-left placements; leader-endpoint instructions) add no function or relationship and are properly treated as depiction conventions. Substantive geometry that is asserted is supported: the branch current sensor straddling the conductor upstream of all three drops (disclosure: "measures total current upstream of the connector contactors"), the isolation strokes on the bus between controller and stations ("isolated local bus"), the direct branch-sensor-to-controller line ("The branch current sensor is an independent safety input"), and the bus branching to the pilot interfaces and contactors ("communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus").
- Abstract is 142 words and adds nothing beyond the disclosure. Background is prior-art characterization and problem statement, which needs no inventor support.

One finding, reported below: FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 both draw a second, dedicated signalling path that carries connector-current reporting to the controller and expressly keeps it "clear of the isolated local bus 106". The disclosure discloses exactly one controller-to-station communication path and never discloses a separate sensor channel, so the separateness is untraced topology; it also leaves FIG. 3, the enlarged view of the same edge controller, with no corresponding input. The fix is a clean deletion that orphans no numeral and leaves the supported description sentence intact.

Note on scope: prior-art characterizations in the Background were not traced to prior_art/ here; that tracing belongs to the later citation review, and the art supplied may be incomplete since no prior-art search was run.

findings.title: FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 assert a dedicated connector-current signalling path separate from the isolated local bus, which the sources never disclose
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, geometry bullet 7 ("A separate line runs from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110...") and figures/FIG-2.md, geometry bullet 6 ("A separate line runs downward from the first connector current sensor 122..."); related text at draft/08-detailed-description.md paragraph beginning "The edge controller 100 communicates with the connector stations over an isolated local bus 106."
findings.detail: Both briefs draw a second controller-to-station signalling path dedicated to connector-current reporting and expressly place it outside the isolated local bus. FIG. 1 says the lines run from each station to the edge controller "each clear of the isolated local bus 106" and that "These lines report each station's measured connector current to the edge controller 100"; FIG. 2 correspondingly branches the bus inside the station only "to the first control-pilot interface 124 and the first contactor 120" and routes the sensor output out of the station on its own line. That is a connection/topology assertion with technical substance: it says the connector-current measurement reaches the controller on a channel other than the isolated bus, i.e. outside the disclosed isolation boundary. The inventor discloses exactly one controller-to-station communication path and names only two things on it. The coupling itself is supported (the controller must obtain the measurement in order to "verif[y] the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor"), but no affirmative passage in the disclosure or in the single USER passage of the conversation states, or implies, a second path separate from the isolated local bus; there is no such passage anywhere in the sources. The same choice also creates a cross-view gap: FIG. 3 is the enlarged view of the identical edge controller 100 and shows no connector-current input at all, so the two dedicated inputs drawn arriving at 100 in FIG. 1 have no counterpart in the enlarged view of that same block.
findings.evidence: Candidate wording, figures/FIG-1.md: "A separate line runs from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 to the edge controller 100, and a like line from the second connector station 112, each clear of the isolated local bus 106. These lines report each station's measured connector current to the edge controller 100." Candidate wording, figures/FIG-2.md: "A separate line runs downward from the first connector current sensor 122, leaves the enclosing rectangle through the right part of its lower side, and ends well inside the lower right of the drawing area." Nearest source passage, showing the gap (input/disclosure.md para. 1 = input/conversation.md USER para. 2): "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." The sources name only the connector interfaces and the contactors on that bus and never mention any second or separate signalling path; the only other statement about connector current is "verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor" (input/disclosure.md para. 2), which affirms the measurement but not any routing.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md delete the entire geometry bullet "A separate line runs from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 to the edge controller 100, and a like line from the second connector station 112, each clear of the isolated local bus 106. These lines report each station's measured connector current to the edge controller 100." In figures/FIG-2.md delete the entire geometry bullet "A separate line runs downward from the first connector current sensor 122, leaves the enclosing rectangle through the right part of its lower side, and ends well inside the lower right of the drawing area." No numeral is assigned to either line, so no entry in draft/numerals.md and no per-sheet numeral list changes (FIG. 1 stays at 8 numerals, FIG. 2 at 7), and the leader-endpoint instructions in both briefs are unaffected. Leave the supported sentence in draft/08-detailed-description.md unchanged: "Each connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured connector current to it." Do not substitute any replacement path (do not re-route the sensor output onto the isolated local bus 106 either), because neither routing is affirmatively disclosed; the block diagrams need not depict the reporting channel.
